official_data_source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) & U.S. Department of the Treasury
credit_risk_attribution: US Sovereign Debt (Zero Default Risk) vs Binance/Tether Private Counterparty Risk
sovereign_vs_crypto_risk_factors: 1. Exchange credit & insolvency risk (Binance custody vs US Treasury full faith and credit).
2. Stablecoin de-peg & reserve backing risk (USDT vs USD legal tender).
3. Operational execution risk (transfer latency, API outages, margin injection delays).
4. Mark-price intrabar spike & liquidation penalty risk.
5. Basis blowout risk (widening Spot-Perp discount during market cascades).
economic_attractiveness_verdict: MARGINAL SPREAD INSUFFICIENT FOR RISK INCURRED: Over the 425-day holding period, unleveraged safe carry (Structure B) yielded +313.12 to +338.56 USDT, underperforming risk-free US Treasury Bills (+610.88 USDT) by -$272.32 to -$297.76 USDT. Even aggressive Structure A (which suffered margin calls and complete cash reserve exhaustion) generated merely +15.35 to +66.24 USDT in excess return over sovereign debt (< 50 bps annualized spread). Bearing crypto exchange counterparty risk and stablecoin de-peg risk for a 0.50% annualized premium is economically indefensible for rational institutional capital.
